note: Changes to PROTOCOL.md or its code checks after pre-registration. The freeze does not hash this file.

deviations.when: 2026-10-13, S0, before any real outcome was read
deviations.what: S0 identity-world criterion changed from an absolute Delta_id(F) > 0.05 to Delta_id(F) >= 0.5 x the oracle-descriptor world's Delta_id(F).
deviations.why: The absolute threshold was set before the synthetic noise level was calibrated. First S0 run: Delta_id(F) 0.044 (fail under the old rule); oracle 0.052. The generic-world check (|Delta_id| < 0.01; observed 0.00002) and F >= R (observed +0.026) are unchanged.
deviations.effect_on_real_data: none; S0 is a synthetic code check

deviations.what: Stacker penalty implemented as 1e-6 x the mean diagonal of the component Gram matrix instead of 1e-6 on raw coefficients; components are not rescaled by route RMS before stacking (RMS is used only in the gate descriptors).
deviations.why: Implementation clarification. Least squares is invariant to component scaling up to the penalty, and a relative penalty of 1e-6 is negligible either way.

deviations.when: 2026-10-13, after S1 and before the freeze and S2
deviations.what: verdict.py fixes operational definitions the protocol left implicit: 'significantly negative' = 95% CI upper bound < 0; V2 applies to the hypothesis pipelines (A' and B non-trivial), B full reported; mechanism-class rule = Delta_id(F) > 0 at p < 0.025, F - F_-know >= 0.5 x Delta_id(F) at p < 0.05, and the CI lower bound of F - F_-genetic <= 0; a functional-genetic claim is SUPPORTED only if that lower bound is > 0.
deviations.why: Removes discretion from the S2 reading. Written after S1 was seen; S1 (fold 0) is development and is never scored in S2.
deviations.effect_on_real_data: none on any estimate; fixes how S2 estimates map to verdicts

deviations.when: 2026-10-13, during S2, before any S2 estimate was written or printed
deviations.what: The frozen `python run.py s2` finished the real S2 pipeline and all 5 relabellings (3247 s), then raised KeyError: 'scores' in run_controls and exited 1 without writing RESULTS.json. stage() passes the dict of Task B pipelines ({'full', 'nontrivial'}) where run_controls expects the non-trivial result. S2 is rerun through run_s2.py, which leaves run.py's frozen bytes unchanged and wraps run_controls to receive rb['nontrivial'] (what the dev-fold smoke test passed). The wrapped path was first run end to end on development fold 0 (`run_s2.py --path-check`, output in tmp/ only).
deviations.why: Engineering defect in a code path S1 never exercised (S1 runs without controls). The only console output of the failed run was elapsed times; no estimate was seen. The computation is deterministic (salted seeds), so the rerun reproduces the same real and relabelled values and remains the single S2 look.
deviations.effect_on_real_data: none on any estimate, arm, population or gate; run_s2.py adds the key 'entry' to RESULTS.json

deviations.when: 2026-10-13, after the S2 verdict (IDENTITY_WITHOUT_METHOD, H1-A' passing), before any Task C number was computed
deviations.what: PROTOCOL.md section 10 designed Task C but left its operational definitions open; TASK_C.md fixes them (truth set, candidate universe, training-only degree and strata, seven arms incl. an added chemical-neighbour target-transfer baseline, admission gate and label, primary contrasts C1 F-Zc and C2 OC-X, decision rule). taskc.py implements it and writes RESULTS_C.json once. Before locking, `taskc.py --count` read annotation counts only (1,148 units, 276 active), and a crash check ran the pipeline on development fold 0 without printing any hit count.
deviations.why: Section 9 permits Task C after this verdict; fixing the definitions before computing removes discretion. The definitions were written after Tasks A' and B were seen, so Task C is exploratory.
deviations.effect_on_real_data: none on Tasks A' and B
